text: {"memo": "Microsoft reported FY2025, for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, revenue of $245.1 billion, up 16% from $211.9 billion in FY2024 and up 7% from $168.1 billion in FY2023. Net income was $88.1 billion in FY2025, or diluted EPS of $3.23, compared with $72.7 billion and $2.72 in FY2024, and $54.9 billion and $1.99 in FY2023. Operating cash flow was about $109.4 billion in FY2025. The Intelligent Cloud segment drove growth, with Azure revenue up roughly 28% in FY2025, while the company maintained high single-digit to low double-digit revenue growth ahead of the year. FY2024 results showed revenue of $211.9 billion, net income of $72.7 billion, diluted EPS of $2.72, and operating cash flow of about $78.6 billion. FY2023 revenue was $168.1 billion, net income was $54.9 billion, diluted EPS was $1.99, and operating cash flow was about $56.8 billion. Margins remained robust, with operating margin around 42% in FY2024 and improved in FY2025. On balance, FY2025 represented a strong year, though Azure growth moderated from the prior year’s 40% pace. View: MSFT remains a premium mega-cap growth-and-diversification compounder, but investors should expect multiple compression if AI infrastructure spending and cloud growth slow."}
